You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The issue stems from the behavior of CommandLine.getOptionValue(String) when accessing the value of an option using its long option name. The failing test creates an option with a short option 'd' and a long option "debug" (via OptionBuilder.withLongOpt), then calls PosixParser.parse() on the command line args. The test asserts the presence of the option using the long option name "debug" which works correctly. However, the issue report says calling getOptionValue("debug") returns null, while getOptionValue('d') (short opt) returns the correct value.

Examining CommandLine.getOptionValue(String) shows it calls getOptionValues(String), which strips leading hyphens from the input, then uses the string "opt" as a key to look up the names map to map to the canonical option key. If names.containsKey(opt) is true, it uses names.get(opt) as the key to look up in the options map for the Option object.

The key difference is in names and options maps. The test setup and parsed CommandLine state likely store options indexed by short option character 'd', but the names map may not have a mapping for "debug" long option to 'd'. Therefore getOptionValues("debug") doesn't find the key in options, returning null.

This is likely caused by the parser or option registration not populating the names map with mappings from the long option to the short option key, resulting in getOptionValue(String) failing with the long option name argument contrary to the documented expectations. The parser correctly recognizes the option with the long option name in hasOption(), but getOptionValue() fails due to the internal maps missing the reverse lookup for long option.

The root problem lies in the parsing or option registration logic that establishes the names mapping and ensures option values can be retrieved by long option name as well as short option character. The test shows usage of OptionBuilder and PosixParser and their interplay resulting in this mismatch.

Recommended investigation includes verifying how the names map in CommandLine is populated during parsing, and whether long option names are entered correctly. Fix should be applied to ensure getOptionValue(String) works with both short and long option names as documented.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
